subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` defaults continue to override later global or per-agent exec security configuration, or should operator config changes invalidate or dominate those persisted session fields?
rationale: Current code, tests, and docs intentionally model `/exec` as durable session state, but the issue describes a real security-policy enforcement concern when operator config changes after that state is written.

options.title: Operator config wins with migration
options.body: Change precedence or versioning so stricter operator exec config invalidates persisted session exec fields, with focused migration/reset tests for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep durable session defaults
options.body: Treat `/exec` as a documented session-level operator shortcut and add clearer reset, doctor, or UI guidance for clearing stale exec defaults.

options.title: Pause until contract is explicit
options.body: Leave this issue open until the session-default contract is explicitly revisited by the security/config owners.

recommendation.title: Operator config wins with migration
recommendation.body: Change precedence or versioning so stricter operator exec config invalidates persisted session exec fields, with focused migration/reset tests for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties this person to the original `/exec` session-default contract and follow-up resolver coverage.
